definitions.gloss: rebuilding; reconstruction; tearing down and building anew
definitions.explanation: The act of demolishing an existing structure and constructing a new one in its place. Different from renovation (リフォーム), which preserves the basic structure.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{建|た}て{替|か}えを{決|き}めた。
examples.english: We decided to rebuild the house.

examples.japanese: マンションの{建|た}て{替|か}え{工事|こうじ}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The apartment building reconstruction work has begun.

examples.japanese: {老朽化|ろうきゅうか}した{校舎|こうしゃ}の{建|た}て{替|か}えに{数年|すうねん}かかる{見込|みこ}みだ。
examples.english: The rebuilding of the deteriorated school building is expected to take several years.

notes:
The noun form of {建|た}て{替|か}える (to rebuild). Refers specifically to demolishing and rebuilding from scratch, not mere repair or renovation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {建|た}て{替|か}え{工事|こうじ} — rebuilding construction
- {建|た}て{替|か}え{費用|ひよう} — rebuilding costs
- {建|た}て{替|か}え{計画|けいかく} — rebuilding plan
- {建|た}て{替|か}えを{検討|けんとう}する — to consider rebuilding

SIMILAR WORDS:
- リフォーム — renovation; remodeling (preserves the basic structure)
- {改築|かいちく} — rebuilding; structural alteration (can be partial)
- {新築|しんちく} — new construction; building from scratch on a new or cleared site
- {修繕|しゅうぜん} — repair; maintenance (fixes problems without replacing the whole structure)

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
{立替|たてか}え (also read たてかえ) means advancing money on someone's behalf — a completely different word. Context usually makes the distinction clear.
